sources.title: Dash Academy curriculum — module 1 manifest row
Dash Academy curriculum — modules 8–17 (hands-on testnet build arc)

claims.text: Module 1 is a 12-minute concepts lesson worth 100 EXP with no prerequisites, whose quiz challenge ID is what-is-dash-platform and whose scope is the two-layer split, developer value, about-a-second payments, concrete buildables, and the course arc.
Dash has two connected layers: Dash Core, the layer-1 blockchain that settles Dash payments, and Dash Platform, a layer-2 application state and structured-data layer.

On Platform, a developer describes application data with a schema (a data contract) and submits signed state transitions that change it; they do not deploy arbitrary user-written code for the network to run.

Platform's two core components are Drive (consensus-backed decentralized storage) and DAPI (a decentralized API with JSON-RPC and gRPC endpoints that lets a client read and write Platform data and query the Core chain without running a node).
A blockchain network gives an app developer decentralized storage and shared state that is not owned by one company's server, plus client libraries that hide blockchain complexity.
Dash payments confirm in about a second: Dash reached transaction finality in little more than a second and offers instant transaction confirmation.
About-a-second confirmation means a seller can accept a Dash payment immediately without waiting for multiple mined blocks, getting fiat-like speed at low cost.

Concrete things a developer can build on Dash include human-readable .dash usernames via DPNS tied to identities, structured application data (data contracts and documents), configurable fungible tokens, document-based NFTs, and Dash payments—exemplified by DashMint Lab, Dashnote, and DashPay.

In this course the learner builds, on testnet, a small end-to-end app: connect to DAPI and make a verified read, derive and fund a Platform address, create an identity, register a DPNS username, publish a data contract, submit and query documents, transfer and purchase documents, create a native token, and charge tokens for document operations.

uncertainties.topic: Prior lesson content covered finality mechanics outside the current manifest
uncertainties.resolution: The committed lesson taught InstantSend, ChainLocks, Tenderdash, and LLMQs. The current manifest forbids them, so the lesson was rewritten to cover the two-layer split and its developer-facing effects without naming those mechanisms.
The manifest phrase 'about a second' is anchored to what-is-dash.md's 'little more than a second'; the lesson names the effect (fast confirmation) rather than any locking or consensus mechanism.

uncertainties.topic: Course build arc has no separate capstone document
uncertainties.resolution: The 'what you will build' section is derived directly from the fixed curriculum modules 8-17 and is described as the course's shared testnet project rather than an invented named app.
